page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with paragraphs numbered in Roman numerals (XXII to XXVI). No margin notes. Bottom: catchword at the right and gathering signature at the centre-left. Faint show-through from the reverse side is visible and not transcribed.

main_text.p: Discernatur etiam summum ius ab æquitate. Etsi enim genere congruunt, quia utroq; probantur recta & damnantur contraria, tamen gradibus differunt propter circumstantias.
Est igitur summum ius cum leges seuere sine mitigatione retinentur, etiam cum propter circumstantiam aliquam probabilis ratio erat mitigationis.
ἐπιεικεια[?] vero seu æquitas est probabilis mitigatio summi iuris in aliqua circumstantia, præsertim in casu, de quo non principaliter lex loquitur.

Et quoniam ἐπιεικεια[?] aut publica est, aut priuata, publicam illam quæ in iudiciis versatur Magistratibus & Iurisconsultis relinquamus, qui sapientissime disputant, utrum iudicandum sit ex scripto iure, an æquitas extra scriptum quærenda sit, priuatam vero, cuius tres sunt gradus, nisi exercebimus, nihil dilectioni erga proximum relinquemus.
Primus gradus est eleganter ferre communes hominum infirmitates, quæ non puniuntur legi[?]bus. De hoc gradu Plinius dixit: Qui vitia odit, homines odit. Nemo enim sine vitiis nascitur

page.notes: The last paragraph (from "Primus gradus" to "nascitur") is struck through with ink lines in the scan; the text is still printed and is transcribed in full. The Greek word ἐπιεικεια is faint and uncertain in both places. "legibus" is partly obscured by the strike-through. A faint word "Dicer" at the lower left looks like show-through or a stray mark and is not transcribed. A stain in the left margin beside XXII is not text. The page has no printed page number or running head; "A 5" is the gathering signature.
